prosperiti-insights.title: #53: Why India’s factories struggle to keep up with the world
prosperiti-insights.description: An Indian factory takes 23% longer to fill the same export order than a Vietnamese factory and pays for 18% more labour-hours to do it.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #130: Why did China slash warehouse robot costs by 70%?
decoding-the-dragon.description: Hai Robotics and Geek+ moved automation off bolted steel and onto bare concrete, and India's warehouses and labour-cost edge are next in line.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #129: Why is China demoting English as its rank hits 86th?
decoding-the-dragon.description: Beijing is quietly stripping English out of its classrooms just as India's whole services economy leans harder than ever on the very same language.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #128: Why has India built just 2.8% of its battery target?
decoding-the-dragon.description: China quietly commoditised the machines that validate almost every battery on earth, and India's own cell ambition leans on them long before it ever leans on Chinese cells.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #127: How did two Chinese firms crack a $3.6bn chip-polishing monopoly?
decoding-the-dragon.description: DuPont and Cabot once owned the slurries and pads inside every chip. Dinglong and Anji undercut them by up to 40%, and India barely features.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #126: How did China cut joint-implant prices by 80%?
decoding-the-dragon.description: China slashed the price of a new hip by roughly 80%, and instead of killing its implant makers it built two global champions. India cut prices too. It got the opposite result.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #125: Why do Chinese pollution monitors cost a third of imports?
decoding-the-dragon.description: China's laser-based emission analysers broke a Japanese-Western hold on price, gave the state a live view of every smokestack, and now the boom that built them is fading.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #124: Why does one Chinese company control 20% of world fibreglass?
decoding-the-dragon.description: China Jushi just posted a 74% profit jump while roving prices sat near record lows, and India buys most of its glass fibre from the very machine doing this.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #123: Why does China sell precision bearings at half SKF's price?
decoding-the-dragon.description: A century-old Swedish, German and Japanese club owned the world's bearings. China's C&U and ZWZ just broke in, and India is buying the result.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #122: Why does China make 98% of the world's cheapest batteries?
decoding-the-dragon.description: EcoFlow and Bluetti turned that cell dominance into a global power-station empire, killed the petrol generator, and left India importing the whole box.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #121: Why does India import 90% of its chip machines?
decoding-the-dragon.description: China's ACM and Kingsemi broke the West's decades-old grip on chip-making machines; India is still importing nearly every tool its new fabs will run on.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #120: Why is China's metro system $650bn in debt?
decoding-the-dragon.description: China built the world's largest metro network in two decades, and the bill has now come due just as India races to copy the model.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #119: How is China selling 100W fast chargers for under $15?
decoding-the-dragon.description: Innoscience turned next-gen power chips into a commodity, made its first annual profit, and now sits alone on Nvidia’s AI power list while India lags.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #118: Why does China make 97% of the world's humanoid robots?
decoding-the-dragon.description: A standing-desk parts maker in Zhejiang quietly halved the cost of motion hardware, and now the same trick is building the muscles of every robot China ships.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #117: Why did China crash silicon carbide from $1,500 to $400?
decoding-the-dragon.description: Having bankrupted the West and captured the market, China is quietly raising the price again, and India still makes almost none of it.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #116: Why does a $40 Chinese drill worry DeWalt?
decoding-the-dragon.description: Firms like Dongcheng and Worx deliver 80% of a premium tool's performance at a fraction of the price, and India barely makes any.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #115: Why did China's sewing king order 2,000 humanoid robots?
decoding-the-dragon.description: The firm behind 6 in 10 of India's sewing machines is now automating the last human step, and cheap-labour garment economies are the collateral.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #114: How did a $1,500 welder crash to $150?
decoding-the-dragon.description: Two Shenzhen firms swapped copper and iron for silicon, hollowed out welder makers from Faridabad outward, and are now being undercut by their own clones.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #113: Why did China's top power-chip maker lose 76% of profit?
decoding-the-dragon.description: China's power-chip champions are winning the price war and losing their own profits, and India's entire EV and solar boom now rides on the outcome.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #112: Why does China build drug-filling machines at half Europe's price?
decoding-the-dragon.description: Two firms, born in a cowshed and a repair shop, now undercut Europe's pharma-machine giants by half, and India's cheap-Ozempic wave runs on their lines.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #111: How does one firm undercut Bosch by 50% and win?
decoding-the-dragon.description: Hengli broke the German-Japanese grip on the hydraulics inside every excavator, and now wants the robot's joints too, while India still imports both.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #110: How is China selling humanoid robots for $16,000?
decoding-the-dragon.description: China has quietly crushed the cost of the precision motors inside every robot's hands, and India, which makes almost none of them, has plenty to worry about.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #109: Why does one Shenzhen firm cool 30% of China's AI?
decoding-the-dragon.description: Envicool commoditised the plumbing that keeps NVIDIA's hottest chips alive, squeezed Vertiv on price, and left India without an answer of its own.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #108: How did China fit 32 lasers into one 3D printer?
decoding-the-dragon.description: China turned metal 3D printing from a lab curiosity into mass production, and India's tiny additive industry is watching from the sidelines.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #107: Why does one firm make 40% of EV safety switches?
decoding-the-dragon.description: A single Xiamen company now sets the price of the switch that guards every EV battery, and India's electric ambitions run straight through it.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #106: Why does China make 56% of AI's optical modules?
decoding-the-dragon.description: The tiny light-based parts that let AI chips talk to each other have become a geopolitical weapon, and India, busy building its own AI data centres, makes almost none of them.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #105: Why does a $300,000 sprayer's job now cost $5,000?
decoding-the-dragon.description: A Guangzhou drone-maker turned China's farm labour crisis into its first profit, and India's own drone dream runs on the same hardware.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #104: Why does China grow 80% of the world's laser crystals?
decoding-the-dragon.description: One company, spun out of a state chemistry lab, now sits inside almost every high-power laser on earth, and India buys the machines but grows none of the crystals.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #103: Why does China's No. 3 e-scooter maker claim 15 million a year?
decoding-the-dragon.description: The 15 million is installed capacity across many plants, not output. The real lesson is that scale followed a market that already existed, not a factory announcement.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #102: Why does UltraTech own 2,024 MW of green power when China's cement giants don't?
decoding-the-dragon.description: UltraTech crossed 2,024 MW of green power because Indian industrial power is priced and regulated to make captive renewables the cheapest unit. China's cement makers face a different sum.

decoding-the-dragon.title: #101: Why did a $15 cutting tool crash to $2?
decoding-the-dragon.description: China's toolmakers have stripped precision machining down to pocket change, and India's factory floors are quietly running on it while our own tungsten sits unmined.

bharatnama.title: #107: Why can't gig workers reach India's ₹1.6 lakh crore safety net?
bharatnama.description: India built rails to route a delivery rider to your door in ten minutes, but still cannot route a working-capital loan to that same rider.

bharatnama.title: #106: Why add 12,000-HP trains to India's 51-kmph tracks?
bharatnama.description: India is world-class at electrifying its railway, near-bottom at running on it, and the new engines fix the wrong half of the problem.

bharatnama.title: #105: Why does 1 in 3 Indian undergraduates study arts?
bharatnama.description: The world thinks India runs on engineers. Its own enrolment data says something stranger, and in the AI age that quirk may be its biggest edge.

bharatnama.title: #104: Why is India’s ₹78,000 crore student-loan boom avoiding income shares?
bharatnama.description: America’s income-share agreements promised to fund learners without debt, then collapsed. India is quietly building the same outcome-alignment on regulated credit rails instead.

bharatnama.title: #103: Why does one leaked paper void 22 lakh Indians' exam?
bharatnama.description: India runs the world's largest exams on a paper model built to leak, while the science that actually makes tests leak-proof stays outside the room.

bharatnama.title: #102: Why does India charge 40% more to insure an EV?
bharatnama.description: India is buying electric vehicles faster than ever, but the actuarial maths behind insuring them is quietly breaking, and the buyer is paying for it.

bharatnama.title: #101: Why is 28% of India's private capex just two firms?
bharatnama.description: After years of waiting, private investment has finally roared back, but almost all of it sits with two conglomerates and their data centres.

bharatnama.title: #100: Why do two states corner half of India's FDI?
bharatnama.description: India stopped being one economy years ago, and its foreign capital keeps choosing the same two or three winners.

bharatnama.title: #99: Why does a fertiliser ministry set India's medicine prices?
bharatnama.description: India built pharma as a chemical industry and bolted safety on afterwards, while no other major drug regulator sits outside its health ministry.

bharatnama.title: #98: Why did India's family offices jump from 45 to 300?
bharatnama.description: India's richest families have stopped being quiet backers of venture funds and started writing the cheques themselves, and it is rewiring who bankrolls Indian startups.

bharatnama.title: #97: Why is India 5th most-spammed despite blocking 27cr daily?
bharatnama.description: India runs the world's most aggressive anti-spam machine, blocks 27cr messages a day, and still ranks fifth on Earth for spam. The fix may be architectural.

bharatnama.title: #96: Why does India buy 1mn tractors, almost none electric?
bharatnama.description: India just became the first country to sell 1mn tractors in a single year, yet the electric ones on its farms you can almost count on one hand.

bharatnama.title: #95: Why does India have just 30 years to grow rich?
bharatnama.description: India has the world’s youngest big workforce and a window that begins shutting by 2040. The dividend is real, but it has to be earned, not inherited.

bharatnama.title: #94: How real is India's ₹3.48 lakh crore welfare saving?
bharatnama.description: India's JAM plumbing now shields more citizens than almost any nation on earth, yet the headline “savings” quietly bank cheap crude and excluded families as efficiency.

bharatnama.title: #93: Why do 54 lakh Indians take one shot at merit?
bharatnama.description: India runs the world's fairest large-scale entrance exams, and the West, which lectures us on equity, is quietly rigging its own.

bharatnama.title: #92: Why does India design 20% of chips but make none?
bharatnama.description: India trains nearly one in five of the world's chip engineers, yet fabricates almost none of the silicon they design, and one state now holds most of the fix.

bharatnama.title: #91: Why do India's banks lend ₹83 of every ₹100 saved?
bharatnama.description: India's lenders have run short of deposits just as China's are drowning in savings nobody will borrow, and both are squeezing bank margins from opposite ends.

bharatnama.title: #90: Why are India's unicorn founders now raising ₹500 crore funds?
bharatnama.description: India's startups were built mostly on foreign money, and now the founders who got rich are quietly funding the next generation themselves.

bharatnama.title: #89: Why is India's 1.4bn consumer market really just 120mn?
bharatnama.description: The pitch says a billion consumers. The data says a top decile the size of Mexico does two-thirds of the spending, increasingly on borrowed money.

bharatnama.title: #88: Why do 6 in 10 Indian women still not work?
bharatnama.description: Female participation has nearly doubled in seven years, yet India still trails Bangladesh, China and the world average, and the gap is fixable.

bharatnama.title: #87: Why can just 23% of India's third-graders read?
bharatnama.description: Finland fixed this by making teaching harder to enter than medicine. India, at 25 times the scale, is betting on something else entirely.

bharatnama.title: #86: Why does India's formalised economy still pay ₹12,000 a month?
bharatnama.description: India has built the world's largest digital tax and payments rails, yet nine in ten of its workers are still informal and the average one takes home ₹12,000 a month.

bharatnama.title: #85: Why does a 60-km Mumbai local cost just ₹20?
bharatnama.description: The world's most crowded commuter railway is priced below cost on purpose, and freight shippers across India quietly pay the difference.

bharatnama.title: #84: Why is ₹892 crore buying land the government already owns?
bharatnama.description: India's tax department is buying prime Mumbai land from a loss-making state phone company, and the only person not in the room is the taxpayer writing the cheque.

bharatnama.title: #83: Who really pays Indian Railways’ 60,000 crore pension bill?
bharatnama.description: India thinks its train tickets fund the pension of the man who once punched them. They do not. The freight shipper does, and when he cannot, the taxpayer.

bharatnama.title: #82: Why is India's bullet train now 83% over budget?
bharatnama.description: The 0.1% Japanese loan is real. That it is free, mostly Japan-funded, or will ever pay for itself is not.

bharatnama.title: #81: Why has a ₹310 crore rural fund committed only ₹218 crore?
bharatnama.description: It buys stakes in venture funds, not companies. Each fund must put at least the same amount into agro and rural businesses that are not pure software. Ten years on, the cheques are concentrated and la

bharatnama.title: #80: Why has India's ₹1,005 crore space fund called only ₹188.93 crore?
bharatnama.description: The first close was real. The money that has moved is not. One cheque is public, two names are still in the dark, and the gap between commitment and cash is the whole story.

bharatnama.title: #79: Why is India buying 40 turboprops but building no jets?
bharatnama.description: A firm order for 40 turboprops exists. A factory needs 200 firm jet orders that no Indian airline has placed yet.

bharatnama.title: #78: Why do just 4% of Indian workers have formal training?
bharatnama.description: India has built the world's largest skilling apparatus, yet most of its workforce is still untrained, and of those who are, fewer than half end up in a job.

biznewsbyjay.title: #83: How did one campus build ₹53,000 crore of deep tech?
biznewsbyjay.description: One Chennai campus has quietly built India's boldest early-stage portfolio, and the reason is a clock that no venture fund is allowed to run.

biznewsbyjay.title: #82: Why does a battery worth half the car write off the whole thing?
biznewsbyjay.description: Indian EV premiums look cheap, even cheaper than petrol in places, but that benign price tag hides a write-off problem insurers are quietly terrified of.

biznewsbyjay.title: #81: Why does India tax a leased EV battery at 18%?
biznewsbyjay.description: Strip the battery out to make the electric vehicle cheaper, and the taxman suddenly treats it as a service, quietly splitting the whole market into winners and losers.

biznewsbyjay.title: #80: Why are India's 300 family offices bypassing venture funds?
biznewsbyjay.description: The families who once funded VCs now sit on cap tables themselves, and Ranjan Pai's rescue of Byju's shows exactly how the power shifted.

biznewsbyjay.title: #79: Why does a ₹2.47 crore trap cost just ₹5 lakh?
biznewsbyjay.description: India built the world's most consumer-protective payment rails, and its own startups quietly turned the very same rails into the cheapest way to keep billing you.

biznewsbyjay.title: #78: Why is ₹2,095 crore being claimed on the Taj's land?
biznewsbyjay.description: The Mumbai Port owns the ground beneath the Taj, the lease ran out in 2001, and the rent bill has quietly climbed in the footnotes ever since.

biznewsbyjay.title: #77: Why does a 1% duty gap route India's gold through Dubai?
biznewsbyjay.description: India's gold bill hit a record last year even as the tonnage fell, and a one-point duty gap is quietly steering the trade to Dubai.

biznewsbyjay.title: #76: Why did a ₹53 crore startup just win Reebok India?
biznewsbyjay.description: The company that grew Reebok 2x in India does not own the brand, and this week it discovered it never had the brand all to itself.

biznewsbyjay.title: #75: Why do Chinese firms now make 45% of India's turbines?
biznewsbyjay.description: The apps of Indian wind used to be Suzlon and Inox. Now the biggest customers have built their own factories, and a Chinese newcomer owns the order book.

biznewsbyjay.title: #74: Why does India have 123mn credit cards but only 57mn users?
biznewsbyjay.description: Mastercard calls India's thin card base a runway. The real growth is small-ticket, small-town, and quietly running on a rail Visa and Mastercard cannot ride.

biznewsbyjay.title: #73: Why are 70% of India's greenest trucks Chinese?
biznewsbyjay.description: The "Make in India" badge sits on a Foton and a BYD, while the costliest parts, and the live telemetry, still route back to China.

biznewsbyjay.title: #72: Why did insurers sell property cover at a 99% discount?
biznewsbyjay.description: For a year, factories bought flood and fire cover for almost nothing. Then Gujarat flooded, and the market found out what it had actually promised.

biznewsbyjay.title: #71: Why did Taj's catering jump 69% but grow just 16%?
biznewsbyjay.description: The 69% headline is mostly an accounting quirk. The real story sits with one Singapore partner and one Tata airline.

biznewsbyjay.title: #70: Why does one AI data centre need 290 diesel engines?
biznewsbyjay.description: The grid can't arrive in time for India's AI ambitions, so the boom everyone calls green quietly runs on diesel.

biznewsbyjay.title: #69: Why is India's 50% gold-loan boom mostly just gold prices?
biznewsbyjay.description: Strip out a 42% rise in the price of gold, and the sector's dazzling growth splits into one lender genuinely winning share and everyone else simply holding heavier collateral.

biznewsbyjay.title: #68: Why did District lose 53 times BookMyShow Live's profit?
biznewsbyjay.description: BookMyShow and Eternal are both burning cash on concerts, but the real prize they are chasing is not the ticket at all.

biznewsbyjay.title: #67: Why did Blinkit write off ₹308 crore of stock?
biznewsbyjay.description: The four store formats everyone noticed are not really an assortment play. They are what happens when the box, and the balance sheet, outgrow the model.

biznewsbyjay.title: #66: Why does India's $7bn lithium milestone raise questions?
biznewsbyjay.description: An Indian company just did something genuinely important and overdue by mining lithium abroad, yet its headline numbers deserve a much closer look.

biznewsbyjay.title: #65: Why does one ₹20,000 crore tank order have three builders?
biznewsbyjay.description: Tata came in lowest, but that only buys it 130 weeks of prototype-building against a state-funded rival, for a fleet that arrives in the 2030s.

biznewsbyjay.title: #64: Why is India's ₹20 lakh crore infra-trust dream still roads?
biznewsbyjay.description: The lobby is selling ships, ports and data centres as the future. Follow the money, and it is still roads and towers, growing far too slowly to get there.

biznewsbyjay.title: #63: Why does India's ₹10,900 crore EV push skip the tractor?
biznewsbyjay.description: India just sold a record ~1.15mn tractors and startups like Moonrider want them electric, but the flagship EV subsidy was never built for the farm.

biznewsbyjay.title: #62: Why has JFE bet its entire India play on one family?
biznewsbyjay.description: Japan's second-largest steelmaker has wired itself into two arms of the Jindal clan, and the reason it is safe to concentrate rather than diversify is the most interesting part.

biznewsbyjay.title: #61: Why is GE handing India 80% of its jet engine?
biznewsbyjay.description: Airbus sourcing has tripled to $1.5bn and America is transferring engine IP, yet India still imports the raw metal the whole thing rests on.

biznewsbyjay.title: #60: Why is Oil India betting big on Haryana's garbage?
biznewsbyjay.description: The State just made city garbage a guaranteed business, and a cash-rich oil PSU is diving in exactly where private capital lost ₹428 crore.

biznewsbyjay.title: #59: Why is half of India's new auto-rickshaws now electric?
biznewsbyjay.description: China owns the electric car race, but it quietly ceded the rickshaw, the cargo three-wheeler and the tractor, and that is exactly where India is quietly winning.

biznewsbyjay.title: #58: Why did silver return 98% but its buyers just 18%?
biznewsbyjay.description: The metal did not quietly replace gold this year. It doubled, crashed, and taught a hard lesson: the channel you buy through decides your outcome more than the price does.

biznewsbyjay.title: #57: Why did Adani Enterprises drop 5% after a CARE AA upgrade?
biznewsbyjay.description: CARE upgraded the debt, not the equity. The lender got safer, the owner got a shrug, and the same company moved two ways in one day.

biznewsbyjay.title: #56: Why did the rupee fall 9% while reserves rose?
biznewsbyjay.description: The RBI pulled in $133bn from the diaspora and reserves climbed, yet the currency barely moved, because the dollar that matters found a new home.

biznewsbyjay.title: #55: Why can 168mn cans still say 'energy' in India?
biznewsbyjay.description: FSSAI ordered one word off the can without a hearing. The four firms that went to court got relief, and the merits wait for 5 November.

biznewsbyjay.title: #54: Why are insurers selling factory fire cover at 99% off?
biznewsbyjay.description: Fire premiums have crashed 28% in a booming economy, and the reason is a price war that quietly hands the bill to you.

rest-of-world-latest-slash.title: AI companies want to embed safety evaluators, but countries need their own
rest-of-world-latest-slash.description: At a Rest of World event in New York last week, speakers explored how countries sidelined by the U.S.-China race can retain some control over safety standards as they adopt models from OpenAI, Anthropic, and others.

rest-of-world-latest-slash.title: The open-source AI platforms vying to become China’s Hugging Face
rest-of-world-latest-slash.description: AI model platforms ModelScope and MoArk are competing to serve Chinese-speaking developers behind the Great Firewall.

rest-of-world-latest-slash.title: South Korea’s AI chip giants are fighting for a bigger role in America’s AI boom
rest-of-world-latest-slash.description: Samsung and SK Hynix dominate the high-bandwidth memory market. Now they are competing to become indispensable to Nvidia, OpenAI, and other U.S. AI companies.
